Why "Known For Something" Beats "Known For Everything"

6 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Since December 2025, Instagram shows users an AI-written summary of the topics it thinks they like ("Lately you've been into…"), and lets them add or remove topics. If nobody can sum up your account in a topic, the recommendation system has a harder time placing you too.

Instagram's "Your Algorithm" tool, opened from the icon at the top right of Reels, lists the interests Instagram has inferred and lets people ask for more or less of each one (TechCrunch, December 2025). It launched in the US first, with a wider English rollout planned. The lesson for creators is plain: platforms sort people and content by topic. A clear topic is easier to sort.

✗ MYTH

Niching down means fewer followers.

✓ REALITY

Niching down means fewer wrong followers. A broad account competes with every creator in Kenya. A focused one is the obvious choice for one group of people, who are also more likely to save, share and buy. You can widen later. It's much harder to narrow a confused audience.

The one-sentence test

Can a stranger describe your account in one sentence after seeing three posts? If it takes a paragraph ("she does comedy, but also cooking, and sometimes church, and some business tips…"), you have a hobby feed, not a brand.

Too broadSharperWho instantly knows it's for them
ComedyMatatu-culture skits for Nairobi commutersAnyone who rides a 46 or a Rongai mat
Business tipsSourcing and pricing for Gikomba mitumba resellersNew resellers on WhatsApp Status
BeautyNatural hair care on a student budgetCampus students in Kenya
FoodKisumu fish recipes for under KES 500Families feeding 4 on a budget
💡 The niche is a person

Your niche is a person, not a topic. "Fashion" is a topic. "A 24-year-old in her first office job who needs outfits under KES 3,000" is a person. When you know the person, ideas come easily: what does she worry about this week? Write that post.

💡 Your niche is now a search term

Since 10 July 2025, public posts from Instagram business and creator accounts (for users over 18) can appear in Google search results unless you switch it off (PPC Land). The words in your bio and captions are now search words. "Nairobi braids" in your caption can be found on Google. "✨vibes✨" can't.

📋 Your one-line niche
I post [TOPIC] for [SPECIFIC PERSON] so they can [RESULT].

Example: I post honest phone reviews for Kenyan students so they can buy the best phone under KES 20,000.
✅ Do this today (under 15 minutes)
⚡ Quick check

What does Instagram's "Your Algorithm" tool (launched December 2025) let users do?

It shows users the topics Instagram thinks they like and lets them adjust them. Recommendations are organised around topics, which is why a clearly describable account is easier to recommend to the right people.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Platforms sort content and people by topic. Make yours obvious.
  2. Pass the one-sentence test: a stranger should sum you up after three posts.
  3. Define your niche as a specific person, not just a subject.
  4. Bio and caption words now work as search terms, including on Google.
